scope: Local script inventory. No implementation, no guaranteed availability, no inferred contents of missing side conversation. Ember and Aivu friendship only.

candidates.name: Soana

identity_source.text: {n}An old dwarf woman, so ancient that she looks like she's been carved from a piece of gnarled driftwood, stands in the middle of the cave. The only decoration visible among her filthy rags is a clay medallion in the shape of a complicated knot.{/n}

hook_source.text: {n}The old woman crosses her arms over her chest.{/n} "Yes. Orso the Terrible is my creation. I used this medallion to control an evil spirit of the Abyss after linking it to the sacred bear, and I forced the spirit to serve good by linking our lives together."

candidates.authored_concept: Experimental new route. Untangle her life-linked Abyss-spirit bargain and restore the forest without erasing her age or culpability.
candidates.constraints: Her destructive protection and sacrifice are core motives; no youthful reskin assumption.
candidates.integration_status: No native romance established by reviewed evidence; any new route must still be checked against installed expansion content.

candidates.name: Areelu
candidates.adult_evidence: Adult mother and long-established researcher; exact current age not required.

identity_source.text: "I thought I had hidden my home well... but I was wrong. They found it. They found us. At that hour, I was there, in the laboratory — that damned laboratory I loved so much! I was absorbed in one of my experiments when the hunters arrived on our doorstep. I was sitting at my desk, recording my observations, thoughts, and calculations, as was my habit. That's when I heard the noise outside. The fight was brief. It barely lasted a moment. By the time I sensed that something was amiss, and hurried out to see what was happening — it was too late. All I could do was cradle the body of my dead child... and cry after their departing soul... 'I promise.'"

hook_source.text: "And when I realized that..." {n}Areelu's voice grows stronger, and a storm rages in her eyes.{/n} "I rebelled. But not against my jailers. Not against those who had murdered my child. Not even against Sarkoris. My uprising was against destiny, death, and the laws that the gods had forced upon our lives. I realized then that I wouldn't be satisfied with simply returning my {mf|son|daughter} to life. I had to shatter this order once and for all, and make it so that neither Pharasma and her lackeys, nor death itself, could ever stand between us. Only by stepping beyond the bounds of what had been ordained for mortalkind, by obtaining powers that rivaled the divine, could we become free."

candidates.authored_concept: Experimental family-boundary review first. A nonromantic alliance concerning fate and loss is supported.
candidates.constraints: Do not turn the native child-replacement/maternal premise into romance; an unrelated adult premise would need separate explicit authorship and audit.
candidates.integration_status: No native romance established by reviewed evidence; any new route must still be checked against installed expansion content.

candidates.name: Jannah Aldori
candidates.adult_evidence: Adult portrayal inferred from Eagle Watch military service and drinking companionship; no numeric age verified.

identity_source.text: "And one last thing. The Eagle Watch has lost a lot of soldiers recently — some were killed, but others simply haven't been seen since the attack. In the chaos that is now {g|Kenabres}Kenabres{/g}, it's next to impossible to confirm anything for sure." {n}Irabeth clears her throat.{/n} "One of the missing fighters is Jannah Aldori, a new recruit in the Watch. She got along well with Seelah and she often went drinking with her. I honestly thought Seelah and Jannah had died together. But now Seelah's returned with you and there's no sign of Jannah. If you learn anything of her whereabouts when you're out in the city, please report back."

hook_source.text: {n}Seelah looks shaken and distraught. Gritting her teeth, she turns away.{/n} "You heard what the Commander said, Jannah. Wait here, and soldiers from Drezen will come for you and take you to prison. And... if it counts for anything, I'm sorry."

hook_source.text: {n}The dead priestess glares at you, green flames raging in her empty eye sockets.{/n} "What have you done to me... How dare you desssecrate my remainsss!" {n}With each word, air from her lungs wooshes out between her ribs.{/n}

candidates.name: Elyanka Camilary
candidates.adult_evidence: Explicit old woman, presently mortal; sixteen describes a past event.

identity_source.text: {n}The old woman raises her chin proudly.{/n} "My name is Elyanka Camilary. I come from a small but ancient {g|Ustalav}Ustalav{/g} family. When I received {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa's{/g} blessing, I was only sixteen. At the time, strange people used to come to our forests. They burnt fires, danced around them, sang in an unknown language, made merry, and feasted on the meat of stags shot illegally in the Camilary woods."

hook_source.text: {n}The old woman answers with ease, but there is bitter disappointment in her eyes.{/n} "My time will come. One day I will become the daughter of {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g}, her adopted child. I will have the immortality and power promised to me. But for now the goddess wants me to remain mortal. This way I can be of more use to the cult, as a messenger who spreads the wisdom of her church. If it were up to me, I would have left this grubby, sweat-reeking, disgusting mortal life many years ago."

candidates.authored_concept: New Trickster encounter with an adult Urgathoa priestess whose native access is Lich-centered.
candidates.constraints: Her desired undeath is not a condition she already possesses. Preserve fanaticism and Septimus conflict.

candidates.name: Herrax
candidates.adult_evidence: Adult succubus and brothel madam portrayal; exact age unstated.

identity_source.text: {n}You are greeted by a succubus whose appearance is striking, to say the least. Her flawless skin, graceful figure, and aristocratic face would have made her a true beauty if not for the terrible, fresh scars. A jagged scar runs across her cheek, cutting through her scarlet sensual lips and under her high cheekbone. Her left eye is a gray cataract surrounded by wounds from some caustic substance. The succubus's wings are tattered rags. Nevertheless, she behaves imperiously and with dignity, and those around her treat her with respect.{/n}

hook_source.text: "Do you mean the former madam of the Ten Thousand Delights or the new one?" {n}The succubus winks with her one working eye.{/n}

candidates.name: Mielarah
candidates.adult_evidence: Adult captain/sorceress portrayal with established career; exact age unstated.

identity_source.text: Starcatcher the Third easily catches the air current and glides forward. Discipline, instilled by the grim sorceress called Mielarah, reigns over the ship. Silent and diligent sailors sweep away the tiniest signs of mess on deck with the eagerness of zealous inquisitors.

hook_source.text: Captain Mielarah responds to the Commander's order with a desperate nod, but with every subsequent minute she passes at the helm, her face grows {d|c4 captain mielara}darker and darker{/d}. As the wind tears the sails, Mielarah's mind struggles with the realization that her dark fate — the curse of the Gravedragger — is creeping up on her. Unable to resist the overwhelming panic, she lets the wheel slip out of her hands, and the ship crashes into the raging waters of Ishiar.

candidates.authored_concept: New voyage route addressing Gravedragger curse and choices aboard Starcatcher the Third.
candidates.constraints: Do not flatten principled captain into innocent heroine: thought-correction and disastrous coercion are also native. Travel outcomes need rescue alternatives.

candidates.name: Hepzamirah
candidates.adult_evidence: Adult nephilim commander and archpriestess portrayal; daughter is kinship, not age.

identity_source.text: {n}Hepzamirah's roar shakes the ground. Her angry eyes flash crimson.{/n} "When I'm finished with you, I will have you chained! You will be dragged behind the army, naked, wounded, and trembling. You will watch as I, daughter of Baphomet, and archpriestess of his cult, take Golarion by the throat. I will bring it to its knees, and make it weep like a wench that's been whipped!"

hook_source.text: "Hiding! They say being the Daughter of Baphomet is a great gift, but, like all of my father's gifts, it was poisoned. That poison is known as mortality. I'm a nephilim, and unlike demons, I must share the fate of the most worthless minions of the Lord of Beasts! Upon death, the souls of all of his slaves are bound here — and I'll remain in this torment forevermore!"

candidates.authored_concept: Experimental rescue from post-death imprisonment and an independently chosen anti-Baphomet alliance.
candidates.constraints: She is mortal nephilim, not ordinary immortal demon. Her revenge pledge is not romance, and gratitude must not be coerced.

identity_source.text: {n}Iomedae's arrival is not the grand affair it was last time — the goddess simply materializes in front of you. Her face is serene, but her eyes look thoughtful. She nods to you in greeting, but does not seem to be in a hurry to speak.{/n}

hook_source.text: "I congratulate you on your victory, {name}, as one warrior to another. Deskari, the self-proclaimed Usher of the Apocalypse, was defeated in the Worldwound, at the entrance to his own realm. History will remember you as the {mf|hero|heroine} who accomplished this feat. But you have the chance to achieve an even greater victory — you can rid Golarion of its bleeding wound once and for all."

candidates.name: Eliandra
candidates.adult_evidence: Woman/high priestess with hundred-year vigil explicitly established.

identity_source.text: {n}The woman's face seems to glow with a radiant light. She looks at you with quiet dignity, and her eyes shine with warmth and wisdom.{/n} "Greetings, herald of Iomedae the Lightbringer! And to your companion as well. I am Eliandra, high priestess of Pulura. I am happy to see a new face in my temple, the first I have seen in all the years of our vigil..."

hook_source.text: "You should honor her request, Champion. Eliandra is one of the most radiant souls I know, and Katair is one of the most loyal and devoted. They have spent a hundred years together with their comrades in voluntary isolation. It would be easy to lose one's clarity of perspective. I do not know mortals well enough to sense whether doubt or despair lives in the hearts of those who dwell in the Fall, but perhaps you can?"

candidates.authored_concept: New route from Pulura vigil and rescue, with a bespoke Trickster access alternative.
candidates.constraints: Katair is explicitly her fellow leader; reviewed evidence does not establish spouses. Avoid assuming a romance from their shared vigil.

candidates.name: Targona
candidates.adult_evidence: Adult angel portrayal; precise age unstated.

identity_source.text: "Unbeknownst to me, I acquired this power... Even immersed in my enchanted sleep, I protected the poor folk who were imprisoned in Areelu's laboratory with me. And Eliandra and Katair did the same at Pulura's Fall. It was their self-sacrifice, so different but always sincere, that protected the temple, not just Pulura's power. The Hand of the Inheritor had long suspected this, but only after speaking to me did he finally realize the truth."

hook_source.text: "Countless times, by whatever means we could think of. Nothing worked. Maybe if we'd had a powerful cleric or spellcaster among us... Then again, seems unlikely if Areelu imprisoned an actual {g|angel}angel{/g} down here so easily, doesn't it?" {n}The elf nods toward the unmoving winged woman.{/n} "We can't even explore the whole laboratory — some of the passages are blocked by barriers that only let demons through."

candidates.authored_concept: Existing RanRomance route extension through laboratory captivity, altered wing, and recovery; not a new route.
candidates.constraints: Healing/restoration and personal choice are prerequisites, not payment for rescue. Angel-specific native continuation needs authored Trickster access.
